about.title: About Me
about.text:
When I was a child, computers felt extremely interesting to me.
For a kid playing outside, it was like another world.
I got closer to it through games. Later, I started trying to understand what was inside.

Back then, the internet and computers were not like today.

payments were a new thing
the internet was expensive and slow
software and games were distributed via discs

In that environment, I became an apprentice at a small computer service.
That was my first real school.

In the service:

I installed Windows
I configured computers
I burned and copied discs
I worked with Paynet and internet services

These services were in high demand at that time.
People even came for simple tasks.
I learned technology in practice there.

Later, during college, I opened a small photo studio.
That was my first independent experience.

I:

took ID photos
edited videos
configured USB modems
copied content from cassette to disc

Through this work, I learned not only technical skills but also how to work with clients.

At that time, I was working with technology, but programming had not yet entered my life.
The reason was simple — there was no such environment.

During the quarantine period, I came across programming courses on YouTube.
From that moment, I started learning this field seriously.

I completed an online course:

HTML
CSS
JavaScript

During the course, I showed good results and was offered a position as a mentor assistant.
It was an important recognition for me.
But I could not take the opportunity because of distance.

Then I switched to self-study.

I:

learned React and Redux
understood backend with Node.js
built independent projects
completed a full stack project

This process was difficult.
There was no clear path.
I had to learn many things on my own.

I started looking for a job. I even passed all interviews.
But I was not hired because I was a part-time student.

That was a difficult situation.

After some time, I started looking at programming differently.
Now it is not just work for me.

I started coding again.

Now:

I enjoy the process
I continue learning

I have seen both the old internet era and today’s fast technology era.

That is why I know one thing for sure:

Knowledge learned in difficult conditions does not disappear easily.

I am still in the middle of the journey.
And I continue.
